standard_prerequisites.statement: Omega^0(A,a) := (A,a) as a pointed type and Omega^{n+1}(A,a) := Omega^n(Omega(A,a), refl a).

standard_prerequisites.name: Pointed types and equivalences of pointed types with a basepoint condition
standard_prerequisites.statement: An equivalence of pointed types must carry the basepoint to the basepoint.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof constructs g : Omega(Omega(A,a),p) ~ Omega(Omega(A,a),refl a) and checks g(refl p) = refl(refl a) at source lines 435-444.

core_obligations: Dispose of the cases n = -1 and n = 0 by the two named inputs, namely the characterization of contractible inhabited propositions and the K property for sets (source lines 428-429).
Use induction and rewrite the claim with the loop-space criterion, so that A being an (n+1)-type becomes Omega(A,a) being an n-type for all a (source lines 430-431).
Apply the inductive hypothesis to Omega(A,a) to reduce the goal to the contractibility of Omega^{n+1}(Omega(A,a),p) for all p : Omega(A,a) (source line 432).
Since Omega^{n+2}(A,a) uses the basepoint refl a, exhibit an equivalence g : Omega(Omega(A,a),p) ~ Omega(Omega(A,a),refl a) carrying refl p to refl(refl a) (source lines 434-437).

Define g(q) as the composite refl a = p `ct` opp p = p `ct` opp p = refl a for q : p = p, show it is an equivalence because it is a composite of the two displayed equivalences, and check the basepoint condition (source lines 438-444).

proof_roadmap.step: Base cases n = -1 and n = 0 from the two cited inputs.
Induction step: reformulate with the loop-space criterion and apply the hypothesis.
Reduce the remaining goal to an equivalence of loop spaces at the two basepoints.
Build g as an explicit composite of equivalences and verify the basepoint condition.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.2.9 at source lines 423-426: A is an n-type if and only if Omega^{n+1}(A,a) is contractible for all a. The proof (source lines 427-445) is an induction whose inductive step is not formal: after reformulating with the loop-space criterion (line 431) and applying the hypothesis (line 432), the goal mentions Omega^{n+1}(Omega(A,a),refl a) while the available contractibility is at Omega^{n+1}(Omega(A,a),p), so one has to construct an explicit equivalence g between the two loop spaces at different basepoints (lines 435-437), define it by whiskering a path q : p = p with the concatenation composite refl a = p `ct` opp p = p `ct` opp p = refl a (lines 438-440), prove it is an equivalence as a composite of two named equivalences (lines 441-443), and check that it carries refl p to refl(refl a) (line 444). The statement says nothing about this basepoint comparison.
